deck_title: Rayleigh-Taylor Atwood number A = (rho2-rho1)/(rho2+rho1) two-fluid buoyant plume law vs naive Boussinesq fixed-inertia rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Lord Rayleigh (1883) & Sir Geoffrey Ingram Taylor (1950) stratified two-fluid Rayleigh-Taylor instability Atwood law (dividing net buoyant force (rho_2 - rho_1)*g by total coupled two-fluid inertia rho_2 + rho_1 = 2*rho_1*(1 + u) so A = (rho_2 - rho_1)/(rho_2 + rho_1) = u / (1 + u), locking a_active / a_RT = 1.0000x across all 17 stations u = (rho_2 - rho_1)/(2*rho_1) in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive Boussinesq fixed-inertia shader (dividing by fixed baseline inertia 2*rho_1, which overshoots buoyant acceleration and gamma^2 growth rate by (rho_2 + rho_1)/(2*rho_1) = 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-layer evanescent potential-flow kinetic energy quadrature.

good_fit: 3D underwater ink drops, volcanic mushroom clouds, oil-water lava lamps, and supernova remnant Rayleigh-Taylor finger animations
Dividing net buoyancy (rho_2 - rho_1)*g by coupled two-fluid inertia (rho_2 + rho_1) via the exact Atwood number A = (rho_2 - rho_1)/(rho_2 + rho_1)
Preventing unphysical supersonic acceleration (> g) when heavy-to-light density ratio rho_2 / rho_1 is large
not_for: Single-phase compressible acoustic sound waves with zero gravity
